enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organization (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. You should write between 450 - 500 words. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity.

questions.enonce_markdown: **g)** Write a letter to your sister explaining how you made your mother angry and the consequences of your actions.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Informal letter: address and date, greeting, opening remarks.
2. What I did: lied about extra lessons, spent the money and went to a party.
3. How mother found out and her anger.
4. Consequences: punishment, loss of trust, and my lesson.
5. Closing: request for her advice, regards, signature.

**Model composition (487 words)**

Government Bilingual High School,
P.O. Box 114,
Bamenda.
14th March 2021

Dear Mimi,

I hope this letter finds you in good health and high spirits. I am fine, but my heart is heavy, and I need to share something with you because you are the only person who always understands me. Please do not laugh at me, and do not tell anybody before you have read it to the end.

You will remember that before school resumed, Mother gave me twenty thousand francs to pay for extra lessons in mathematics and English. She had saved the money for months by selling vegetables, and she told me, "Do not waste it, because this is my sweat." I promised to use it well. However, when I came to Bamenda, some new friends invited me to a birthday party at a nearby hotel. I told myself that one outing would do no harm, so I spent half of the money on clothes and entertainment. When the money was almost finished, I could not pay for the lessons, and I did not have the courage to tell Mother the truth.

Instead, I made a serious mistake. When she called me on the telephone, I lied that I was attending the lessons every evening. I even said that the teacher was very impressed with my work. My lie worked for three weeks. Then, last Saturday, Mother unexpectedly came to Bamenda to bring me foodstuff and decided to meet my teacher to thank him. The teacher, who was very surprised, told her that I had never attended a single lesson.

You cannot imagine how angry Mother was. She did not shout, which was even more frightening. She simply stared at me with tears in her eyes and said, "I have been lying awake at night to pay for your future, and this is how you repay me?" Then she took me aside and told me that she was ashamed of me. I wished the ground could open and swallow me.

The consequences have been very painful. She has refused to give me any pocket money for the whole term, and she took my phone away. She will not allow me to visit home during the holidays until my results improve. Worse still, she says that she can no longer trust me, and that hurts me more than any punishment. Even Father has stopped talking to me.

I have learnt a hard lesson. A lie only hides the truth for a short time, and honesty is the only way to keep the trust of the people who love us. I have promised Mother to work very hard, and I have already started attending the lessons, which I now pay for with my own savings.

Please write to me soon and advise me on how to win back Mother's confidence. Give my love to Father and to our little brother Neba.

Your loving brother,
Fon

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organization | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Using the wrong layout: a letter to a sister is informal, with the sender's address and date, a greeting, a closing and a signature.
2. Explaining the anger but forgetting the consequences, or the reverse.
